- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply downward correction of 2–5% for 3–7 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model frequently underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% for next 5–10 days.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, forecast should not continue falling; adjust upward if sentiment turns positive.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; use 10–15 day moving average or sentiment-weighted smoothing to reduce noise.
- When sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.67/0.33), model tends to overreact; dampen forecast by 1–2% for 7–14 days to avoid overcorrection.
